sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 8592 of 2023

Applicant :- Manaendra Alias Naina Tiwari
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. Deptt. Home, U.P. Lucknow

Counsel for Applicant :- Rama Pati Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anshuman Singh,Pradeep Kumar
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Counter affidavit and rejoinder affidavit filed today, are taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Mr. Anshuman Singh, learned counsel for informant,
learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
3. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was married about two years ago on 22.5.2021 and sufficient dowry was given.
It was also given subsequently, on demand of dowry, the daughter of the informant was killed by poisoning.
4. Learned counsel for applicant argues that in the FIR, general allegations on demand of dowry was made.
He further draws attention on the inquest report wherein applicant himself informed the police with regard to death of the daughter of informant.

He further draws attention towards Manaendra Alias Naina Tiwari vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195778143/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further argues that as per the analysis report, the cause of death is poisoning.

He argues that apparently the victim has committed suicide and there is no averment on record neither in FIR nor any of the statements of witnesses to demonstrate that immediately or prior to the death,
the victim was subjected to mental or physical cruelty on demand of dowry.
He, thus, argues that applicant who has no criminal antecedent and is languishing in jail since 09.01.2023, should be enlarged on bail.
He further argues that the other co-accused namely the brother of the applicant has already been enlarged on bail.

5. Learned counsel for informant as well as learned A.G.A. opposes the bail application by arguing that death of the daughter of the informant has occurred within two years of the marriage and, thus,
the presumption of Section 304 B IPC has to be discharged by the accused.

He argues that the demand of dowry is clearly established from the information contained in the FIR as well as from the statements of the witnesses and, thus, the bail application deserves to be rejected.
6. Considering the submissions made at bar, prima-facie, the FIR discloses that sufficient dowry was given at the time of marriage.

Allegations with regard to further demand of dowry is also in the FIR as well as in the statements of witnesses, it is not denied that victim died on account of poisoning which is also fortified on the medical analysis report, however, the allegation with regard to harassment immediately before the death which is sin qua non under Section 304 B IPC is prima-facie absent, this Court cannot go into the sufficiency of the evidence at this stage, the presumption of Section 304B IPC, is to be seen at the time of trial and cannot be a criteria for determining of grant or rejection of bail.

Considering the fact that the applicant is in custody since 9.1.2023 and has no criminal antecedents, prima-facie there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant enlarged on bail can adversely affect the trial.
The trial has not started yet and none of the witnesses have been examined.
Keeping in view the said, the applicant is held entitled to be released on bail.
7. However, the trial Court is directed to expedite the trial preferably within a period of 12 months.

8. Let the applicant Manaendra Alias Naina Tiwari be released on bail in Case Crime no.0554 of 2022 under Sections 498A and 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 of D.P. Act, 1961 at P.S.- Beniganj, District- Hardoi on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each of like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
